description.value: The study examined whether fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex alters error-monitoring activation, stop-task performance, and clinical outcomes in adolescent boys with ADHD, compared with an active neurofeedback control targeting the left parahippocampal gyrus.

design.value: A single-blind randomised controlled trial investigating the effect of fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex in boys with ADHD compared to an active control group receiving neurofeedback of the left parahippocampal gyrus. Participants completed pre- and post-neurofeedback fMRI stop-task assessments.

task_name.value: fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex

task_description.value: The protocol consisted of four 1 h to 1.15 h sessions within a 2-week period, totalling a maximum of 14 neurofeedback runs of 8.5 min each. Each run consisted of six activation blocks of 40 s separated by 30 s rest blocks. During activation blocks, participants viewed a rocket video representing neurofeedback of the target region and were asked to move it toward space using any strategy. After the last neurofeedback run, participants completed a transfer run without feedback.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to move the rocket toward space using any strategy they could. Minimal instructions were given.

stimuli.value: A video of a rocket during activation blocks and an image of a dolphin during the initial rest block; a score from 0 to 10 was displayed after each activation/training block.

task_performance_measures.value: fMRI-NF performance, based on the distance travelled during each run

task_description.value: A choice reaction time task in which participants responded as fast as possible to arrows pointing left or right. In 20% of trials, a stop signal followed the go signal and participants had to inhibit their response. The task consisted of 156 go trials and 40 stop signals, with stop signals appearing about 250 ms after the go signal. A tracking algorithm adjusted the interval between go and stop signals to produce 50% successful and 50% unsuccessful inhibition trials.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to respond as fast as they could to arrows pointing left or right and to inhibit their response when a stop signal appeared.

stimuli.value: Arrows pointing left or right followed in some trials by a stop signal.

description.value: Real-time fMRI neurofeedback acquisition consisting of runs of 8.5 min. The neurofeedback signal was updated every MRI repetition time, i.e. every 2 s, using the BOLD response in a target ROI relative to a white-matter reference ROI. A T1-weighted structural image and a two-volume EPI localizer image were collected at the start of each session.

description.value: Participants underwent an fMRI tracking stop task before and after neurofeedback training. Details of the acquisition are available in Alegria et al. (2017) and the supplementary material.

The fMRI data underwent realignment, motion correction, smoothing, global detrending and spin-excitation history correction. The mean BOLD signal was extracted from target and white-matter reference ROI masks for real-time neurofeedback.
